name: Aon
description: Aon is the second-largest listed insurance broker by revenue. Its Risk Capital segment places commercial insurance and reinsurance for clients and is paid by commissions and fees, and Human Capital sells employee health and benefits brokerage, retirement consulting, pension administration and investment advice. It also earns interest on premiums held for clients. Revenue was $17.2 billion in 2025 with 6% organic growth; the single largest client was about 1% of revenue. It sold most of the NFP Wealth business for $2.3 billion in October 2025 (pre-tax gain $1.2 billion).

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC 6411. Aon reports two segments, Risk Capital (broking) and Human Capital (health brokerage plus pension and investment consulting), so about a third of revenue is benefits and consulting work.

hq.note: 15 George's Quay, Dublin 2 (FY2025 10-K cover); incorporated in Ireland

businessLines.name: Commercial Risk Solutions
businessLines.how: Corporate clients pay fees and insurers pay commission out of premium when Aon places their property, casualty and specialty cover; renews annually and moves with premium rates and exposure.
businessLines.description: Insurance and specialty broking, global risk consulting, captives management, affinity programs.

businessLines.name: Reinsurance Solutions
businessLines.how: Insurers pay brokerage or fees when Aon arranges their reinsurance; insurance-linked securities work earns placement fees.
businessLines.description: Treaty and facultative reinsurance broking, strategy and technology group, capital markets (insurance-linked securities).

businessLines.name: Health Solutions
businessLines.how: Employers pay commissions and fees for designing and placing group health and benefit plans, renewing yearly; revenue rises with covered headcount and plan cost inflation.
businessLines.description: Health and benefits consulting and brokerage, consumer benefits, compensation and talent advisory.

businessLines.name: Wealth Solutions
businessLines.how: Pension plans and corporates pay advisory and administration fees, and investment clients pay fees tied to assets advised; market levels and asset inflows matter.
businessLines.description: Retirement consulting, pension administration and investment consulting.

brands.name: NFP (wealth arm sold Oct 30, 2025 for $2.3B proceeds)
brands.share: Remaining NFP businesses sit inside Human Capital and Risk Capital; separate revenue not disclosed in the text read
